ev.q: Enterovirus or HPeV serotypes were specified for 1,171 (72%) NESS reports.
During July 2007--December 2008, a total of 3,192 (3%) of the 108,798 reports sent to NREVSS were positive for enterovirus.
CVB1 was the most commonly detected enterovirus identified in 235 (17%) of 1,171 specimens tested
A total of 1,632 enterovirus or HPeV detections were reported to NESS during this period
The five most common enterovirus serotypes accounted for 54% of total detections with a known serotype in 2006--2008
In 2007 and 2008, CVB1 was the predominant serotype detected, accounting for 24% and 19% of overall detections, respectively.
NESS, initiated in 1961, is a passive, voluntary surveillance system that monitors laboratory detections of enteroviruses in the United States.
This report describes trends in nonpolio enterovirus and HPeV detections during 2006--2008

methods_quotes.q: Enterovirus serotyping is performed by sequencing the genome region encoding the VP1 capsid protein
All participating laboratories that reported at least one enterovirus-positive specimen were included in this analysis.
It collects the number of enterovirus tests and the proportion that are positive, by specimen site and collection date
